correctness.rationale: Properness confines each color class to one multipartite part. For a vertex in part i, its open neighborhood is exactly the union of all other parts, so a neighborhood color is unique exactly when a singleton color class lies in another part. This gives the iff condition of at least two witness parts, the minimum formula, the interval spectrum, and the counting formula. Inclusion-exclusion for singleton fibers is standard and was reconstructed explicitly. Exhaustive direct checking through order six agrees with every structural and counting formula tested.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification on a canonical graph class, not merely a minimum-value computation. The same structural lemma simultaneously yields the exact PCF chromatic number, the full feasible color-count spectrum, and a closed surjective-coloring enumerator. It sharpens the known complete-bipartite endpoint into an all-multipartite theorem and supplies reusable counting data for a currently active coloring invariant.
